chunks: ʿAlī ibn Mahziyār, from al-Ḥasan, from al-Qāsim ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Aḥmad, from Yūnus ibn Ẓabyān, who said:
I was sitting with Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, and he said: “What do the people say about the souls of the believers?”
I said: They say that they are in the crops of green birds, in lamps beneath the Throne.
So Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: “Glory be to Allah! The believer is more honorable before Allah than that his soul should be placed in the crop of a green bird.

O Yūnus, when Allah, the Exalted, takes the believer, He places his soul in a form like his form in the world. Then they eat and drink, and when a newcomer arrives to them, they recognize him by that image which he had in the world.”

key_terms.أَرْوَاحِ: souls; the immaterial selves of the believers discussed in their post-death state
key_terms.الصُّورَةِ: image or form; the recognizable appearance by which they know one another
key_terms.الْعَرْشِ: the Throne; the lofty realm beneath which the lamps are said to be
key_terms.الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: the believers; those whose souls are the subject of the narration
key_terms.حَوَاصِلِ: crops; the internal pouch of birds, mentioned here as a rejected view
key_terms.رُوحَهُ: his soul; the believer’s soul after death
key_terms.قَالَبٍ: form; a likeness or bodily mold resembling the worldly form
key_terms.قَبَضَهُ: takes him; meaning Allah takes the soul at death

ai.seo_question: What happens to the souls of المؤمنين after death according to Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith describes the state of the believer’s soul after death and rejects the view that it is placed in the crop of a green bird. Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام teaches that the believer’s soul is placed in a form resembling its worldly form, in which the believers recognize one another. The narration is significant for Shia teachings on barzakh and the dignity of the believer before Allah.
